title: Normal Takeoff and Basic Airwork
summary: Normal takeoff, area departure, scanning, turns, speed changes, and introductory stall work.
overview: This event introduces the first full contact-phase maneuver set in the sim. You will practice normal takeoff procedures, local area departures, integrated visual scanning, turn patterns, level speed changes, and power-on stall recognition while continuing to build trim discipline, coordination, and basic energy management.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion items
studyNotes.summary: Focus on smooth takeoff mechanics, disciplined scan habits, and staying ahead of the airplane as configurations and maneuver demands change.

items.text: The normal takeoff is flown in three phases: takeoff roll, rotation, and initial climb.
Lineup priorities include:

children.text: Switch to tower about 200 feet prior to hold short.
Request takeoff using local SOP, then taxi into position only after clearing final.
Run the Lineup Checklist from memory and hold at PROBES ANTI-ICE if told to wait.
Confirm crosswind direction before brake release.

items.text: Key takeoff cues include:

children.text: At 60 KIAS, verify minimum torque and normal fuel flow.
At 90 KIAS, rotate smoothly to about 7 to 10 degrees nose high.
After liftoff, confirm two positive rates, raise gear below 150 KIAS, and raise flaps above 110 KIAS.

items.text: Common errors include improper rudder use, incorrect rotation timing, over-control, and missed gear or flap calls.
Departure procedures begin with being number one for takeoff and complying with runway-specific tower instructions.
General VFR departure rules include:

children.text: No turn prior to 300 feet AGL.
Climb at 180 KIAS and level at 200 KIAS until clear of Class D.
Accelerate to 240 KIAS once outside the local restrictions.

items.text: Be prepared to brief and fly the standard departure options used in this event:
The goal is not just navigation accuracy, but also timely radio changes, altitude compliance, and clean energy management after takeoff.
The integrated scan combines outside visual checks with inside instrument cross-checks to prevent fixation and maintain aircraft control.
In VMC, your eyes should be outside roughly 80 to 90 percent of the time.
A complete scan should include:

children.text: Outside left, center, and right attitude and traffic checks.
Inside attitude and performance instrument checks.
Continuous area clearing before and during maneuvering.

items.text: Do not fixate on one item. Scan rate and sequence should adjust to workload and traffic.
Turn Pattern trains smooth, coordinated turns at increasing bank angles while maintaining altitude and airspeed.
Level Speed Change teaches how trim, power, and configuration changes interact as the aircraft transitions between cruise and landing configurations.
Power-On Stalls simulate departure-type stalls and emphasize recognition, relax-max-level-ball recovery, and coordinated control inputs.
Across all of these maneuvers, the common themes are proper clearing, trim usage, coordinated flight, and preventing fixation on one instrument.
